summary: MetComm.Net LLC argues for continued eligibility of Managed Internal Broadband Services (MIBS) in the E‑Rate program, opposing conversion to an hourly billing model and proposing cost‑effectiveness safeguards. The comment argues that Managed Internal Broadband Services (MIBS) should remain available to small schools and libraries, should not be restricted by size, should be limited by function rather than applicant size, should use a standardized deliverables list to prevent bundling of ineligible services, and should not be replaced by Business Maintenance and Installation Contracts (BMIC). MetComm proposes a standardized, flat‑rate managed internal broadband services (MIBS) framework with clear deliverables, audit procedures, and non‑discriminatory treatment of incumbent vendors.
